cards.text: Job's story has been a LONG road, friend, and we're on the last stretch. The LORD has finished speaking to Job. Now He turns to Eliphaz the Temanite, one of Job's friends.

cards.question: The LORD tells Eliphaz that He's pleased with him and his two friends.
The LORD tells Eliphaz that he and his two friends have not spoken about Him ___, as His servant Job has.

cards.text: The LORD tells them to take seven bulls and seven rams to His servant Job and sacrifice a burnt offering for themselves. Friend, that is NOT a sorry text in the group chat.

cards.question: The three friends will bring their burnt offering to Job. What does the LORD say Job will do for them?
The LORD says that after Job prays for his friends, He will deal with them according to their folly.

cards.text: So Eliphaz and his two friends, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite, go and do as the LORD told them. Three grown men bringing fourteen animals over to Job, and I can't carry ONE cookie box across my bakery without dropping crumbs.

cards.question: Job prays for Eliphaz, Bildad and Zophar. What does the LORD do with Job's prayer?

cards.text: Job prays for the very friends the LORD just called out. And THEN, friend, hold on to your apron, because the LORD restores Job's prosperity.

cards.question: After Job prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and ___ his former possessions.

cards.text: DOUBLED, friend. DOUBLED. Then all of Job's brothers and sisters and everyone who knew him before come and eat with him in his house.

cards.question: Job's family and old friends comfort him over all the adversity the LORD had brought on him. What does each one give him?

answers.text: A piece of silver and a gold ring
A young lamb and a jar of oil
A new robe and a pair of sandals

cards.text: Now look at what Job owns: 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen and 1,000 female donkeys. And I used to think a drawer full of dust was a lot to count.

cards.question: The LORD blessed Job's latter days more than his first.
Along with all those animals, Job also has ___ sons and ___ daughters.

cards.text: Job names his daughters Jemimah, Keziah and Keren-happuch. And in all the land, no women can be found as beautiful as Job's daughters.

cards.question: Job gives his three daughters something among their brothers. What is it?
After all this, Job lives 140 years. How far down his family line does he get to see?

cards.text: And so Job dies, old and full of years. After everything he went through, friend, that's how Job's story ends.

findings.problem: Card 1 only says the LORD finished speaking to Job and turns to Eliphaz. Nothing on it hints at how the LORD feels about Eliphaz, so this true or false card is a coin flip, not a reasoned pick. Card 1 needs a setup the baker can reason from, or the question should change.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The wrong answers "briefly" and "loudly" aren't believable as what the LORD faults the friends for, so the card gives itself away. They should be plausible ways of speaking about God that are still clearly not the meaning of "accurately."

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: "Job's family and old friends" turns the text's "prior acquaintances" into friends. In Job, "friends" points to Eliphaz, Bildad and Zophar, so this can confuse the two groups. Card 11 already had it right with "everyone who knew him before."

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke says a drawer full of dust seemed like a lot to count, as if Job's herds are more. But dust is the thing you can't count, so the comparison runs backwards and a stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.
